name: San Pedro Square Market
angle: A meeting point when everyone wants something different.
description: The market groups food businesses in one destination. Use it as a flexible meeting point, with each person checking their chosen vendor rather than assuming every counter follows the building’s hours.
timing: The official footer lists Sunday–Thursday 11am–10pm and Friday–Saturday 11am–midnight. Another image on the same page differs; confirm the day and vendor directly.
planning: Make the meeting point precise: name a vendor or entrance. “At the market” can leave a group searching across multiple spaces.

name: San José Museum of Art
angle: The useful difference between a Friday and every other day.
description: The museum’s published schedule gives Friday a later closing time. That makes the day of the week a meaningful part of a downtown art plan, rather than treating “museum night” as something available every evening.
timing: Published schedule: Tuesday–Sunday 11am–6pm; Friday until 9pm. Check the admissions page for exceptions and event terms.
planning: Read the exhibition and event listings separately. An evening programme and ordinary gallery admission may have different conditions.

name: The Tech Interactive
angle: Let the actual programme set the plan.
description: This science and technology center also has an IMAX Dome Theater. The exhibition visit and a particular film are different reasons to go, so choose which experience anchors your visit before arranging the rest of the day.
timing: Consult the dated operating calendar and the separate IMAX schedule; a film listing does not establish gallery hours.
planning: Treat a short museum visit and a full film screening as different time commitments. Leave room for the programme you actually choose.

name: Hammer Theatre Center
angle: Build the evening around the performance.
description: The SJSU-operated theatre sits on Paseo de San Antonio between Second and Third Streets. Its calendar is the useful starting point: choose the performance, then make a realistic plan around its arrival and start times.
timing: Dates and times depend on the scheduled production.
planning: Read the event’s own description before choosing a seat. A venue name tells you little about the format of a particular performance.

name: San Jose Civic
angle: The seat map is part of the decision.
description: The Civic is one of the venues represented by San Jose Theaters. Start with the exact event and its seating configuration, because a building’s general capacity does not tell you what the room will look like for your show.
timing: Check the official event page for doors, start time, and admission requirements.
planning: Keep door time and performance time in separate notes. Allow for the venue’s entry process rather than planning to arrive at the first scheduled minute.

name: San Jose Improv
angle: A comedy plan needs more than a comedian’s name.
description: The club occupies the historic Jose Theater. Its downtown location connects it with the wider evening district, but the practical details belong to the specific show: date, seating, age policy, and any additional requirements.
timing: Use the official show listing for times, age limits, and purchase conditions.
planning: Check whether the price shown covers the whole visit. Any minimum purchases or other conditions should come from the current listing, not an old review.

name: MACLA
angle: Free gallery time has a real closing time.
description: MACLA is a contemporary arts space grounded in the Latinx experience. Its regular gallery hours and its performance programme are separate opportunities, so an evening event should not be mistaken for a standing late-night gallery schedule.
timing: Gallery: Wednesday–Sunday noon–5pm, plus special appointments. Gallery admission is free.
planning: For a short visit, focus on the current exhibition. For a performance, check the event page and its seating arrangements.

name: Anno Domini
angle: An art stop that can fit after work.
description: The gallery publishes both exhibition dates and ordinary opening hours. Those two pieces of information make a more useful plan than a generic gallery recommendation: first verify that a show is on, then choose an opening window.
timing: Thursday and Friday noon–7pm; first Fridays 5–9pm; Saturday noon–5pm. Free admission.
planning: An opening reception and an ordinary gallery visit have different rhythms. Decide whether you want the event or time with the exhibition itself.

name: California Theatre
angle: A historic room, with a specific performance in mind.
description: This restored 1927 theatre is part of San Jose’s performing-arts landscape. The building gives the visit context, while the particular opera, concert, or presentation determines the schedule and ticket requirements.
timing: Performance-dependent; consult the presenting organization and official event page.
planning: Choose the performance first and place nearby food or gallery stops around it. A fixed curtain time should be the anchor, not an afterthought.

name: San Jose Stage Company
angle: Make room for a whole production.
description: The Stage produces live theatre in San Jose. A production deserves a different kind of planning from a brief gallery stop: check the run dates and performance details before deciding what else belongs in the evening.
timing: Check the current season and the selected performance date.
planning: Read the production description and any content guidance before booking. The title alone is rarely enough to know whether a show fits your group.

name: SoFA Market
angle: A flexible food stop between fixed plans.
description: Visit San Jose describes SoFA Market as a food hall with several local eateries and vendors. Its South First Street address makes it a useful point to consider alongside nearby arts venues, without treating every vendor as interchangeable.
timing: Confirm individual vendor hours directly; the directory does not establish a common closing time.
planning: If dinner sits between a gallery visit and a show, decide how much time is really available. Choose the vendor after checking its current service arrangements.

name: Haberdasher
angle: A later opening window, clearly stated.
description: Haberdasher’s official site describes a walk-in bar model and publishes a weekly schedule. That makes it a possible evening stop rather than a daytime fallback. Group arrangements need a separate check with the business.
timing: Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday 5pm–midnight; Friday–Saturday 5pm–1am; closed Monday–Tuesday.
planning: The site gives different group-size thresholds in different sections. Confirm arrangements directly for a group instead of treating either threshold as a guaranteed reservation policy.

name: Nirvana Soul, Downtown
angle: Be specific about which coffee shop.
description: Nirvana Soul’s location page distinguishes its shops. This profile refers to the downtown San Jose location, giving you a precise place to compare with the rest of a South First Street plan.
timing: Check the Downtown listing for current hours; other locations have their own schedules.
planning: Use the exact location when sharing a meeting point. A brand with several shops can otherwise send two people to different addresses.

name: City Lights Theater Company
angle: Look one street beyond South First.
description: City Lights is on South Second Street. That is a useful distinction in a district often described through South First: use the actual venue address and the production’s information when arranging your evening.
timing: Performance-dependent; read the selected production’s visit information.
planning: Check runtime and intermission details for the actual show. They determine whether a later meal is realistic; another production’s timings are not a reliable substitute.

name: Roy’s Station
angle: A daytime meeting point with a family history.
description: Roy’s describes its coffee shop as occupying the site of Grandpa Roy’s former Mobil station. Its published early closing times make it a start-of-day or weekend stop, rather than an assumption for an after-work coffee.
timing: Monday–Friday 8am–2pm; Saturday–Sunday 8am–3pm.
planning: Put this stop before a later museum visit if you want both. The café’s closing time is the tighter constraint on many afternoons.

name: Shuei-Do Manju Shop
angle: A specific tradition, not a generic sweets stop.
description: The city’s tourism reference identifies Shuei-Do with manju, and the Japantown Business Association lists its Jackson Street address. This is a chance to learn the name and context of what a shop makes, rather than flattening the neighborhood into a list of snacks.
timing: Confirm current opening hours and selection directly with the shop.
planning: Availability is not established by an online directory. If you are planning around a particular item, ask the shop instead of relying on a photograph from a previous visit.

name: Japanese American Museum of San Jose
angle: Give the neighborhood’s history its own time.
description: The museum is a place to engage with Japanese American history, alongside a visit to the surrounding neighborhood. Its limited afternoon opening window makes it an anchor for a planned visit rather than a last-minute evening stop.
timing: Thursday–Sunday noon–4pm, with listed holiday closures. Published adult admission: $12.
planning: Choose time for the museum first, then fit other stops around it. If your schedule begins after closing, save the interior visit for another day.

name: Jtown Pizza
angle: Move the meeting point off Jackson Street.
description: Jtown Pizza’s official site places it on North Sixth Street. It gives a neighborhood plan a food destination beyond Jackson Street and a specific address to share when people are arriving separately.
timing: Use the official location listing for current service hours.
planning: For a group, confirm seating and dietary requirements directly. An online menu is a starting point, not a guarantee about seating or allergen handling.

name: Nichi Bei Bussan
angle: Spend time with materials and design.
description: Nichi Bei Bussan’s own site presents fabrics, clothing, gifts, and home goods. It offers a way to approach the neighborhood through materials and everyday objects, with its store history providing a separate thread to explore.
timing: Check the store’s current contact and visiting information.
planning: Leave room to look closely. A shop visit can be the purpose of an outing, rather than a hurried gap between food stops.

name: Kogura Company
angle: A neighborhood shop to put on the actual map.
description: The Japantown Business Association lists Kogura Company among the district’s specialty shops. Its Jackson Street address belongs in a compact neighborhood plan, with the business itself the source for current stock and opening hours.
timing: Current hours are not established by the association’s listing; confirm directly.
planning: Treat the association listing as an address reference. Product selection, opening exceptions, and any special services require a more specific source.
